description: Jerard 'Jay' Jackson, 28, was found hanging from a tree near Michigan's Electric Forest festival. Police ruled it a suicide before the autopsy was done. His family — and the evidence — tell a different story.

faqs.answer: Jerard 'Jay' Jackson was a 28-year-old Black man from Illinois who attended the Electric Forest music festival in Rothbury, Michigan in June 2026. His body was found hanging from a tree in a wooded area near the festival grounds on June 30, 2026.
faqs.question: Who was Jerard 'Jay' Jackson?

faqs.answer: Michigan State Police said Jackson called troopers to his campsite to report an alleged criminal incident involving a friend. Troopers determined no crime occurred. Jackson was last seen leaving the festival alone at 10 AM. His body was found the next day. MSP preliminarily ruled it a suicide with 'no indication of foul play.'
faqs.question: What did police say happened?

faqs.answer: Jay had no diagnosed mental health conditions. His phone was taken/left behind by friends. Both front doors of his rental car were found open. Someone attempted to access his bank account two hours after he disappeared. His friends returned to Illinois without him while he was still missing. The family says the 'mental health crisis' narrative was fabricated to cover up drug use.
faqs.question: Why does the family dispute the suicide ruling?

faqs.answer: As of August 6, 2026 — more than five weeks after Jay's death — the official autopsy report and toxicology results have NOT been publicly released. MSP says the investigation is 'active and ongoing.'
faqs.question: Has the autopsy report been released?

faqs.answer: No. No persons of interest have been named. According to Conor Prettyman, he has never been interviewed by detectives regarding the matter.
faqs.question: Has anyone been charged or arrested?

leadParagraph: The body of Jerard 'Jay' Jackson, a 28-year-old Black man from Illinois, was found hanging from a tree in the woods near Michigan's Electric Forest festival on June 30, 2026. Michigan State Police ruled it a suicide within hours — before the autopsy was completed, before toxicology results came back, and before body camera footage from the troopers who were the last people to see him alive was made public. Five weeks later, the autopsy still hasn't been released, no one has been interviewed by detectives, and his friends returned to Illinois without him. His family says nothing about the official story adds up.

methodology: This investigation is based on extensive review of public records, official MSP press releases, local on-scene reporting by Oceana County Press, interviews published by Atlanta Black Star with Jay Jackson's family members (aunt La Toya Neal and stepfather Sean Phillips) and friend Conor Prettyman, community reporting by Stage Hoppers, coverage by Billboard, The Grio, Chicago Defender, and BIN News Network, and public social media posts including Prettyman's Facebook group posts and the family's public statements. UnTelevised Media attempted to independently verify all claims and clearly notes where allegations remain unconfirmed by investigators. No autopsy, toxicology, or body camera footage has been released as of publication date. No FOIA requests were filed as part of this initial investigation.
title: Hanging in the Woods: The Death of Jerard Jackson and the Investigation That Isn't
